newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures drift to mixed close.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures drift to mixed close.

text.p: IMM currency futures drifted to a mixed close after busy morning turnover slowed.

Traders said most nearby futures cut modest losses and edged up toward day's high on what appeared to be small-size shortcovering from dealers and banks after the morning's probe lower proved limited and fleeting.

Sentiment still appeared to favor the downside in currencies after February U.S. jobs figures did little to alter perceptions that the U.S. economy remains strong and inflation controlled, and traders said the bias toward higher U.S. interest rates down the road also stayed intact.

Non-farm payrolls rose 339,000 versus forecasts for up 230,000. The jobless rate fell to 5.3 percent, as expected. Manufacturing jobs fell 2,000, and January's original 271,000-job rise was revised down to a 247,000-jobs rise.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.25 percent to $12.09 from $12.06 and compared to forecasts for up 0.4 percent. The workweek rose to 35.0 hours against 34.6 hours forecast.

"On the nonfarm numbers, the dollar went really nicely bid," said a floor broker. "But wage pressures were in-line... (and) I think a 25-basis-point hike is figured into the market. So I think it's a win-win situation for the dollar."

"The dollar's very, very strong. I don't care what anybody says," said another floor broker early Friday afternoon. "Recovery of the bond and stock markets didn't help any rallies in currencies either."
"I think short-term the dollar has a little bit to go," Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist, Bank of Montreal, told Reuters Financial Television.

He mentioned the 1.7350 to 1.75 dollar/mark levels as "not unrealistically" high and also said market consensus is that the Federal Reserve probably will not hike rates in March but might tighten credit in May.
"I don't think anybody feels the Fed has to act off these numbers," agreed a third floor broker. "The economy's in decent shape with no inflation."
"There's no floor yet here," added a fourth currency broker. "We're going to keep going (down) until we find it."

Sterling futures stayed down, with brokers tying its weakness partly to a technical correction and to crosses versus mark and Swiss franc. They also cited ideas U.K. rates might stay put rather than rise before the U.K. election.
Yen fell on technicals and renewed worries about Japanese financial system after news of another brokerage scandal.
June currency futures become new lead months on Monday.

March yen ended down $0.000052 at $0.008214, marks eased $0.0001 to $0.5832, Swiss francs rose $0.0003 to $0.6760, sterling fell $0.0134 to $1.6018, Can dollar lost $0.0024 to $0.7311, Aussie dollar ended flat at $0.7873, Mexican peso rose $0.000950 to $0.124850.
